Feature.Description:
Connection state and device information of a TP-Link Tapo network camera.
The server talks to the camera over the local network only, using the standard ONVIF (TCP 2020) and RTSP (TCP 554) interfaces authenticated with the camera account (Tapo app: Camera Settings > Advanced Settings > Camera Account). No TP-Link cloud account is used.
Verified model: Tapo C232 (firmware 1.9.1). Other Tapo cameras exposing the same ONVIF/RTSP interface (e.g. C200, C210, C220, C225, C230) are expected to work but are not verified. Features of this server: - TapoCameraController (this feature): status, device information, reset. - VideoCaptureController: still snapshots and fixed-duration video recordings. - PanTiltController: pan/tilt movement and presets (only offered if the camera supports PTZ).
Status values (see property Status): 0: Not Connected - the camera could not be reached; use Reset to reconnect. 1: Idle - connected, no camera operation in progress. 2: Running - at least one camera operation (snapshot, recording, movement) is in progress. Snapshots and recordings may run concurrently with each other and with movements. 3: Error - a camera operation failed; use Reset to recover. Commands of all features are rejected with InvalidInstrumentStatus while the status is Not Connected or Error (except Reset).

Command.Description:
Re-establish the connection to the camera and return the server to the Idle state. Use this after the status became Error or Not Connected.
Status required to execute this command: any Status after this command finishes If it completes normally: Idle If the camera cannot be reached: Not Connected (CameraCommunicationError is raised)

Property.Description: Status of the camera connection. 0: Not Connected, 1: Idle, 2: Running, 3: Error (see the feature description for details).
Device information reported by the camera via ONVIF.

DefinedExecutionError.Description: The camera could not be reached or returned an error. The message contains details.
